title: Provider-neutral tracker seam with a GitHub adapter
summary: Adds a new `tracker` module that defines the provider-neutral seam between the factory and a work tracker: the `Tracker` trait, its data types, the ready rule (`pick`/`dispatchable`), the finishing writes (`finish_run`/`require_capabilities`), and an in-memory `FakeTracker` double. Alongside it lands the first real adapter, `github_tracker`, which drives GitHub Issues and Projects v2 through the installed `gh` CLI: pure functions build each argv and GraphQL payload, pure parsers read each response, and a `GhRunner` trait (real or scripted) executes one `gh` invocation per request. Writes are refused unless the runner carries an explicit identity, and a blocked state posts its cause comment before moving the status.

nodes.label: Factory engine
nodes.subtitle: run loop, not in this diff
nodes.summary: The caller that will use the tracker seam: pick one ready item, then write its state and recap. It is unchanged here; the new module is the seam it will call through.

nodes.label: Tracker trait
nodes.subtitle: read_items / write_state / write_recap / capabilities
nodes.summary: The provider-neutral interface. `read_items` returns a `ReadOutcome`; `write_state` records a blocked cause before moving the status; `capabilities` states what the tracker can do rather than assuming it. Object-safe, so the engine can hold a `&dyn Tracker`.

nodes.label: Tracker data types
nodes.subtitle: WorkItem, WorkItemId, WorkState, Capability
nodes.summary: The value types the seam moves: `WorkItemId` (`provider:repo#item`), `WorkItem` with status, closed flag and blockers, `WorkState` with its `BlockedCause`, and `Capability`/`TrackerCapabilities` for the capability report.

nodes.label: Ready rule
nodes.subtitle: pick / dispatchable
nodes.summary: Kept out of every adapter: an item is dispatchable when it is open, its status is ready, and every blocker is closed. `pick` returns the first dispatchable item, `NothingReady`, a typed list of skipped items, or `Unknown`.

nodes.label: Finishing writes
nodes.subtitle: finish_run / require_capabilities
nodes.summary: Checks the needed states and the recap against the tracker's reported capabilities, then writes the state and the recap, stopping at the first failure and naming the step that failed.

nodes.label: FakeTracker
nodes.subtitle: in-memory double
nodes.summary: An in-memory `Tracker` that records every call as plain data and does no I/O. Tests script its read outcome, capabilities and failures, then assert on the recorded call order.

nodes.label: GitHubTracker
nodes.subtitle: Tracker over gh
nodes.summary: The first adapter. Each request is one `gh` invocation: pure functions build the argv and GraphQL payload, pure parsers read the response. Reads verify the project's status field and options, then page through items; writes resolve the project item id and mutate the single-select field.

nodes.label: GhRunner
nodes.subtitle: run(argv, stdin) -> stdout
nodes.summary: The one place a process is spawned. `RealGhRunner` pipes stdout/stderr on their own threads, feeds stdin, and kills the child after a timeout (60s default). `identity()` is the explicit builder identity; without it the tracker refuses every write.

nodes.label: Payload builders
nodes.subtitle: read_items_payload, mutation_payload, comment_payload
nodes.summary: Pure functions that pin the GraphQL query text and variables for each request: the paged item read with its skip-status search string, the project status read, the item-id read, the field mutation, and the comment body.

nodes.label: Response parsers
nodes.subtitle: parse_items_page, parse_project_status, parse_item_id
nodes.summary: Pure parsers over the `gh` stdout. A malformed item that is not in the ready status is kept as a skipped `unreadable:` item so one bad non-ready item does not fail the page; a malformed ready item fails the read.

nodes.label: gh CLI
nodes.subtitle: installed command-line tool
nodes.summary: The installed `gh` program the real runner spawns. It carries the token and performs the HTTP calls.

nodes.label: GitHub Issues & Projects v2
nodes.subtitle: GraphQL and REST
nodes.summary: The remote system of record: project items, their status field options, issue blockers, and issue comments.

edges.label: pick, finish_run
edges.summary: The engine reaches the tracker only through the trait, so the adapter stays swappable.
The trait's signatures are built from the seam's value types.

edges.label: read_items
edges.summary: The ready rule reads through the trait and never filters by status inside an adapter.

edges.label: capabilities, write_state, write_recap
edges.summary: The finishing writes check capabilities first, then write state and recap in order.

edges.label: implements
edges.summary: The double implements the same trait the real adapter does, so tests exercise the seam without I/O.

edges.label: implements
edges.summary: The GitHub adapter is the first implementation of the seam.
Every request's argv and JSON body come from a pure builder.
Every response is read by a pure parser before it becomes a `WorkItem` or a write result.

edges.label: one gh invocation per request
edges.summary: The adapter is a thin loop over the runner; the runner is the only process boundary.

edges.label: spawn, stdin, timeout
edges.summary: The real runner spawns `gh`, feeds the payload on stdin, and kills it after the timeout.

edges.label: GraphQL / REST
edges.summary: `gh` performs the actual calls to GitHub under the configured token.

views.title: Tracker seam and its first adapter
views.summary: The new provider-neutral seam, the ready rule and finishing writes that sit on it, the in-memory double, and the GitHub adapter that drives `gh`.

views.title: Inside the GitHub adapter
views.summary: How one adapter request is assembled and read: pure builders and parsers around the single process boundary.
